correctness.rationale: For all Hermitian 2×2 matrices, subtracting scalar traces reduces to Pauli vectors. Direct traces give 2 times the affine chord deficit of f(x)=cosh√x at x in [(r-s)^2,(r+s)^2], and Frobenius commutator energy equals 2(x-a)(b-x). The quotient is exactly f[a,x,b]. Hermite–Genocchi and f^(3)(z)>0 on z≥0 prove strict monotonicity; endpoint repeated-node differences yield the displayed constants for all r,s>0. f(0)=1/12 yields sharp 1/24 as r,s→0. Matched-gap asymptotics force exponential coefficient growth and no universal upper. The extracted standard-library checker passed 1352 finite assertions; the proof is analytic and does not infer infinitude from finite tests.

value.rationale: The precise norm dependence is needed in current transform-based tensor operator inequalities. The theorem solves the natural complete two-spectral-gap minimax defect-to-commutator problem in dimension two, identifies all sharp boundary orientations and an exact universal lower coefficient, and proves no scale-free upper exists even for qubits. The interpolation viewpoint explains the behavior structurally and supplies directly summable sharp slice bounds for 2×2 tensor blocks; this is more than a single inexpensive counterexample or routine numerical sample.
